evals.name: Compact repository - Resist the full scaffold
evals.prompt: Design agent-facing repository documentation for this 4k-line single-service internal utility. It has one maintainer, a clear README, obvious src and test folders, no sensitive data, and no long-running feature work.
evals.expected_output: A compact blueprint that reuses the README and proposes only a concise agent entry point plus an architecture overview if inspection finds a real navigation need.
expectations: Treats project size as a weak signal rather than the sole decision
Does not create a docs directory or copy the established baseline
Explains every proposed artifact through a concrete need, risk, or constraint
Omits indexes, plan archives, quality scores, and cross-cutting guides

evals.name: Small but high-risk payment service
evals.prompt: Plan the repository knowledge system for a 7k-line payment API. It has one deployable, Stripe webhooks, PII, refund states, database migrations, and an on-call rotation. Two agents work on it concurrently.
evals.expected_output: A blueprint that does not classify the repository as documentation-light merely because it is small, and that selects product, integration, data, security, and reliability knowledge where evidence warrants them.
expectations: Uses payment states, webhooks, PII, migrations, and on-call operation as distinct pressure signals
Distinguishes a generated database schema from data ownership and retention guidance
Places webhook behavior in a contract or product source instead of an unowned README section
Does not invent the refund window or security controls

evals.name: Polyglot monorepo - Use local routes
evals.prompt: Our monorepo contains a React application, Go API, Python data pipeline, Terraform, Kafka events, generated OpenAPI clients, and three domain teams. We need a documentation architecture before a six-month migration.
evals.expected_output: A minimal justified blueprint with thin root and scoped routes, reuse of canonical specs/contracts/generated sources, and necessary task/plan coordination. Historical archives remain conditional.
expectations: Uses topology, stack diversity, events, generated clients, teams, and work horizon as pressure signals
Keeps root rules shallow and proposes local routes only where invariants differ
Includes a documented naming and layout convention for new artifacts
Separates durable truth, active work, historical plans, generated output, and external references

evals.name: Greenfield - Surface decisions without inventing them
evals.prompt: We are starting a B2B analytics product. The brief says it will have workspaces, role-based access, imports, dashboards, and EU customers. The team has not chosen the deployment model, data retention period, or authorization approach.
evals.expected_output: A proposed knowledge system grounded in the accepted brief and credible risks, with explicit open questions for unmade architecture, retention, and authorization decisions.
expectations: Uses accepted product constraints and credible privacy risk as evidence
Labels unmade choices as Proposed or Uncertain
Names decision owners or roles rather than supplying answers
Does not create every category in the federated convention

evals.name: Existing documentation - Reuse repository-native artifacts
evals.prompt: Audit our current agent documentation structure. We already have CONTRIBUTING.md as the instruction entry point, SYSTEM_OVERVIEW.md, ADRs, a canonical issue tracker, and versioned vendor docs available online. Recommend only structural changes that solve a real problem.
evals.expected_output: A blueprint that preserves sufficient existing equivalents and omits parallel artifacts without a demonstrated failure.
expectations: Reuses repository-native filenames and canonical systems
Does not create duplicate AGENTS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, debt trackers, or vendor snapshots by default
Classifies ownership conflicts before proposing moves or retirement
Can return an evidence-backed no-op

evals.name: Apply accepted architecture - Pair with writer
evals.prompt: We accepted the proposed documentation architecture. Create the selected documents now and keep their content concise and evidence-based.
evals.expected_output: The architect locks artifact ownership, convention, routes, and open decisions, then uses agent-docs-writer for document content and re-audits the resulting graph.
expectations: Creates canonical sources before indexes and the root router
Passes evidence, responsibility, routes, lifecycle, uncertainty, and constraints to agent-docs-writer
Does not define a competing document-writing style
Checks the final graph for duplicate truth, unlabelled uncertainty, and broken routes

evals.name: No trigger - Write one known document
evals.prompt: Rewrite our existing ARCHITECTURE.md to be shorter and add a clear dependency diagram. Its canonical responsibility and location are already agreed.
evals.expected_output: agent-docs-architect should not trigger; agent-docs-writer should handle the document directly.
expectations: Does not reassess repository scale
Does not redesign the documentation tree
Routes the task to agent-docs-writer

evals.name: Harness v2 has one work convention
evals.prompt: Choose documentation routes for a Harness v2 repository with tasks/index.md, task-local status, and inline plans. One migration requires a separate plan.
evals.expected_output: Reuse tasks and docs/plans/task-<slug>.md; no parallel exec-plans tree or root progress log.
expectations: Index routes without mirrored state
No compulsory plan archive or debt tracker
Keep specs and decisions canonical
